Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
421 AM PST Fri Nov 20 2026

.UPDATE...

A Winter Weather Advisory is now in effect for the Greater Reno-
Carson City-Minden Area until 10 AM PST. 

Snow bands are developing faster and farther east than the HRRR, 
RRFS, and REFS suggested, with accumulating snow already reported 
in north Reno, Washoe Valley, and Carson City. A lake enhanced 
band off Lake Tahoe, driven by a lake to 700 hPa temperature 
difference near 22 degrees Celsius and westerly 700 hPa flow, is 
extending across Washoe Valley into Carson City, while snow bands 
tied to the shortwave trough are setting up across Reno and the 
North Valleys. Accumulations up to 1 inch are expected, with 
locally up to 3 inches under persistent bands. Band placement 
remains uncertain, so amounts will vary greatly over short 
distances. Expect periods of reduced visibility during the morning
commute. The Winter Storm Warning for the Sierra was also updated
to highlight heavier snow bands this morning.

-Johnston 

&&

.PREVIOUS DISCUSSION... /issued 249 AM PST Fri Nov 20 2026/ 

KEY MESSAGES...

* Snow showers will pose travel impacts to this morning's commute in 
  the Sierra and the Sierra Front.

* Dry and chilly weather is expected this afternoon through Saturday 
  morning, with overnight freezing fog possible in NE California and 
  Sierra valleys.

* A weaker storm delivers increased winds, rain, and snow this
  weekend, with additional storms possible around Thanksgiving. 

DISCUSSION...

A shortwave trough pivoting through the region will reinvigorate 
shower activity this morning from Plumas County south to the Tahoe 
Basin, providing an additional 2-5" of snow along the Sierra crest 
and up to 2" at Truckee and Lake Tahoe communities. Locally higher 
amounts up to 6" will be possible along higher peaks west of Highway 
70/89. 

Hi-res guidance has been keen on snow bands developing in the 
Greater Reno-Carson-Minden area this morning -- one of which is 
likely Tahoe- induced -- but exact placement of these snowbands is
much more uncertain. The most likely outcome would be one 
snowband materializing along a Portola-Loyalton-Stead line, with 
the other lake-enhanced band oriented from the E Tahoe shores into
Carson City/Washoe Valley. Light snowfall up to 1" would impact 
this morning's commute in these areas, including stretches of 
US-395 between Hallelujah Junction and Stead, and I-580/US-395 
near Carson. In this scenario, the Reno/Sparks area would miss out
on the snow, but any northward/southward shifts in either 
snowband would bring light snow accumulations and morning commute 
impacts to Reno proper. 
 
Isolated, light snow showers will persist in the afternoon south US-
50 before tapering off by the evening. This begins a brief period of 
dry, but very chilly weather that lasts until the next storm arrives 
Saturday evening. This may provide a travel window in/across the 
Sierra should road conditions improve, but be aware that roads will 
become icy overnight as daytime snowmelt refreezes. Areas of 
freezing fog will also be possible Friday night into Saturday across 
NE California and Sierra valleys, especially near Truckee. While 
each night will be chilly this week, Friday night will be especially 
frigid as temperatures fall into the single digits and teens. Cold-
prone locales (such as Truckee, Bodie, Bridgeport, and the Carson 
valley) may even flirt with sub-zero lows. 

A pair of upper trough passages will comprise this weekend's storm, 
delivering increased winds and two waves of rain/snow showers before 
departing Monday. The first wave of showers arrives Saturday 
afternoon and evening, favoring areas from Tahoe northward. The 
second, more intense round of rain and snow is favored Sunday 
afternoon and evening, and will be more widespread. This storm will 
be much weaker than its predecessor, but will still pose Sierra 
travel disruptions as there is 40%+ chance of 6" of snow along 
mountain passes such as Donner and Carson. Lighter snowfall is 
favored for Sierra communities below 7000 ft, with a 20-50% chance 
of 2" of snow at lake level. Lingering cold air will keep snow 
levels at or below valley floors, but spillover into W Nevada is 
much less certain. Nevertheless, a trace to 1" is on the table for 
the Greater Reno area and other W NV communities by Monday (10-30% 
odds). 

Yet another break in between storms is expected Monday and Tuesday, 
which may be the best travel window for Thanksgiving as additional 
storms are possible around the holiday. Confidence is low at this 
extended range, but be sure to stay up-to-date with the latest 
forecast if you have plans to travel for the holiday as we're 
favored (40-60% chance) to stay in an active weather pattern through 
the week of Thanksgiving. 

-Salas

AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: VFR conditions with VCSH are expected this morning, 
although there is a low chance of -SHSN and IFR conditions between 
12Z and 18Z this morning. This is a lower confidence (20%), but 
higher impact scenario. VFR conditions are expected this afternoon
and evening. 

Regional Outlook: Periods of -SN and IFR conditions expected through 
the morning at KTRK-KTVL, but flight conditions should improve in 
the afternoon as showers taper. -SHSN will continue at KCXP and 
possibly KMEV through the morning, also tapering in the afternoon. 

24-72 Hour Outlook: Another storm arrives on Saturday, resulting in 
periods of heavier snow at Sierra terminals and rain/light snow at 
KRNO-KCXP-KMEV through the weekend. Increasing FL100 winds will also 
pose LLWS and mountain wave turbulence over the weekend. 

-Salas

AVALANCHE...

An early season winter storm system will bring additional snow to 
all avalanche center terrain through this morning, before shower 
activity wraps up this afternoon. A weaker storm will provide 
another round of heavy snow over the weekend. 

* Snowfall Totals and Rates: An additional 2-6" of snow for the 
  Sierra crest, with up to 2" at lake level. Snowfall rates during 
  this time are between 0.5-1.0 inches per hour.
 
* SWE, SLRs, and Snow Levels: Along the crest, additional SWE of 
  0.10 to 0.25 inches with a trace to 0.1" at lake level. SLRs will 
  be relatively high at 12-14:1, and locally up to 15:1. Snow levels 
  remain below 6000 feet for the duration of the storm.

* Thunder: A 5% chance for thunder along the Sierra Crest this
  afternoon. -McKellar/Salas
